name_reason: Follows global naming convention data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: data_fd2_ prefix, battle domain (battle-core stat table), descriptor 'enemy_data_table' reflects both content (per-enemy stat records) and data type (array/table). No Ghidra address residue in the name. The trailing '_table' correctly conveys the array nature; no domain ID is embedded that could be mistaken for residue.
purpose: Read-only enemy stat table (68 entries) consulted on battle spawn and combat to provide each enemy template's base stats and XP reward.
logic_summary: const enemy_data[68], 10-byte stride (680 bytes, .object3). Indexed by (enemy portrait id - 0x44) via accessor fd2_get_enemy_data_entry @ 0x4E4FF, which returns base + idx*0xA (&entry.race_id). On battle spawn the runtime char init multiplies HP/MP/AP/DP/DX fields by the enemy level; on kill, exp_reward (+9) is multiplied by the victim level to award XP (scaled by damage fraction if the target survives). hp at +2 is read as a 16-bit word (MOVZX); the other stat fields are single bytes. Verified via read_memory (first entries match the C initializer byte-for-byte) and decompile of accessor + 4 readers.
datatype: const enemy_data[68]  (struct enemy_data, 10-byte stride, total 680 bytes)
element_semantics: Per enemy template (struct enemy_data, 10 bytes): race_id+0 (uint8), class_id+1 (uint8), hp+2 (uint16, base HP scaled by level on spawn), mp+4 (uint8), ap+5 (uint8 attack), dp+6 (uint8 defense), dx+7 (uint8 dexterity/hit), mv+8 (uint8 movement), exp_reward+9 (uint8 XP granted on kill, x level). All 10 bytes are mapped (the earlier 'unmapped 10th byte' note was an artifact of treating the +2 u16 hp as two separate bytes).
comment_original_issue: Source comment listed only 3 readers (fd2_init_runtime_char_for_battle, fd2_execute_attack_damage_calculation, fd2_apply_damage_and_award_xp) but the accessor has 4 callers; fd2_calculate_combat_hit_outcome (0x29F72) was missing. Field layout was described inline without per-field offsets.
notes: is_const confirmed: only xref to 0x61AF9 is a [DATA] read from fd2_get_enemy_data_entry; no writers (also defined const in src). Ghidra data plate at 0x61AF9 was null (verified via run_script_inline reading PLATE_COMMENT); created a concise plate via cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,...) reflecting the src conclusions (MCP set_plate_comment fails for data per project_ghidra_data_plate_mechanism). Live Ghidra symbol name byte-identical to current name. No logic changed; comment-only src edit confined to this symbol's block.
